summary:
The ACES Act of 2025, Pub. L. 119-32, directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to procure a National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine study concerning the prevalence and mortality of cancer among certain former active-duty military aircrew. The Act does not amend the United States Code, create a benefits presumption, or appropriate funds; it establishes a study-and-report requirement.

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary, not later than 30 days after enactment, to seek to enter into an agreement with the National Academies under which the National Academies will conduct the required study. The Secretary must finalize that agreement not later than 60 days after entering negotiations with the National Academies. If the Secretary fails to meet that 60-day finalization requirement, the Secretary must submit a report to the Senate and House Committees on Veterans’ Affairs explaining the failure and estimating the finalization date, and must provide briefings to those committees at least every 60 days thereafter until the agreement is finalized.

Section 2(b) specifies the scope of the study. The National Academies must identify exposures associated with the military occupations of covered individuals, including exposures relating to chemicals, compounds, agents, and other phenomena. It must review the literature to determine associations between those exposures and overall cancer morbidity, overall cancer mortality, and increased incidence or prevalence of specified cancers: brain; colon and rectal; kidney; lung; melanoma skin; non-Hodgkin lymphoma; pancreatic; prostate; testicular; thyroid; urinary bladder; and any other cancers the Secretary, in consultation with the National Academies, determines appropriate. The study also must determine, to the extent possible, the prevalence of and mortality from those cancers among covered individuals using available data sources, which may include Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, and service-specific health care and administrative databases; the National Death Index maintained by the National Center for Health Statistics of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; and the study conducted under section 750 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021.

Section 2(c) requires the National Academies, at the conclusion of the study, to submit a report containing the study results to the Secretary and the Senate and House Committees on Veterans’ Affairs. Section 2(d) defines “covered individual” as an individual who served on active duty in the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps as an aircrew member of a fixed-wing aircraft, including specified aircrew roles and any other crew member who regularly flew in a fixed-wing aircraft.
